title: Prove a sharp two-epoch dirty-fanout gap: 7 versus 9 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

A dirty three-row single-value fanout has exact total cost **7**, while every same-tree echo costs **9**, when directed ADD prices change across its one common-value call. More generally, the unrestricted optimum remains 7 for every real M>=3, while every same-tree echo costs 2M+3. This is a scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

```text
cheap before: ADD(1,0), ADD(2,1)
cheap after:  ADD(2,0), ADD(1,2)
other ADDs: M >= 3; complete common call P0: 1

ADD(2,1), ADD(1,0), ADD(2,1),
P0,
ADD(1,2), ADD(2,0), ADD(1,2).
```

Both three-ADD words realize the same restored-dirt involution through different cheap directions. The all-word lower bound uses the inherited four-ADD dirt floor, then characterizes the intersection of the two cheap matrix groups. Three rows are the smallest size for this separation under the declared exactly-one-P0 contract. The ratio of the same-tree bill to the unrestricted bill is unbounded as M grows.

RossRichardson's #3121 supplies the stationary tariff theorem and explicitly excludes changing prices. This contribution changes that hypothesis; it does not audit or contradict that theorem. Credit RossRichardson #3063, 1337isnot1337 #1944/#1968, anthonylei #774, ofennell-quipex #759 and the retained echo/forest lineage. The elementary three-ADD identity and shortest-path algorithms are classical. Only `research/two-epoch-dirty-fanout/` is added.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19592119).

## Evidence

Before, the stationary forest formula does not determine the changed-epoch optimum. After, a written all-width proof and exact independent finite checks establish seven against the complete forest bill nine at M=3.

At head `61215d260af77caf6f6edaa4c4be055737520e5a`, local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64 passes:

- All 168 invertible three-by-three binary preparation matrices and all 24 legal cut maps at each of M=1,2,3,6,11. Every shortest-distance witness and all 2,016 directed Bellman inequalities per price are checked. All three rooted trees are enumerated.
- All 4,368 literal input assignments at widths one through three, with independent arbitrary dirt and common source, plus thirteen boundary/semantic controls. M=1 recovers the stationary four-ADD control.
- A separately implemented complete truth-table state search, importing no primary or predecessor executable, covers all 1,344 states and 8,232 transitions and obtains total seven.
- Both normal and optimized runs of both checkers, every registered command, metadata/source pins, AST compilation, function-length checks, staged whitespace, exact committed bytes/modes and source-history ancestry. Each of the four registered commands was timed locally below 0.05 seconds, within its 60-second timeout. These are timeout observations, not a speed comparison.
- The official nine-file export passes integrity checks. Both direct checkers pass normally and under optimization from a read-only Git-free export. Generated normal/optimized receipts agree and bind all seven package-file hashes. No receipt is handwritten.

Exact reproduction from the repository root; another CPython 3.12 path may be substituted:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -X dev -W error -B research/two-epoch-dirty-fanout/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -X dev -W error -B research/two-epoch-dirty-fanout/independent.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-epoch-dirty-fanout
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-epoch-dirty-fanout --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Expected markers are `PASS_TWO_EPOCH_DIRTY_FANOUT`, `PASS_INDEPENDENT_TWO_EPOCH_FANOUT`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Standard library only. Scientific replay invokes no predecessor executable. Canonical main was refreshed before commit and remains `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The result uses exactly three arbitrary-dirty XOR rows, one preserved common source and exactly one call at row zero. It prices the specified two-epoch contract. More calls, helpers, changing sources, adaptive programs and other target interfaces are separate problems. Its forest comparison concerns the stated children-before-parents preparation and literal reverse, not every use of a forest as a lower-bound witness.

No actual caller is shown to have these complete prices. Physical source access, coefficient/frame changes, routing, ownership, precision/storage, restoration, head return and the full recursive invoice remain unpriced. No supplier admission, selected cold replay, native build, Lean or Docker run, new kappa or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. All five selected framework assumptions remain. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. All registered mathematical checks ran locally; none is deferred to CI.

## Open next questions

- Bind one actual owner/cut to complete two-epoch tariffs and price both spellings of the involution, including all source, frame, routing and restoration charges. No physical price assignment is supplied.
- Characterize changed-epoch price matrices for which the combined-edge same-tree optimizer remains exact. Start with one fixed small caller and compare its cut-matrix optimization with its tree bill; unrestricted cut complexity and physical price changes remain blockers.

## Related open work

- [#7183](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7183) prices three-row independent radical demands over R16 with two insertions and stationary directed-cycle tariffs. This result uses one binary common value and changes prices across one cut. It reuses none of that package and computes no common numerical optimum.
- [#7265](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7265) gives a four-row orthogonal Boolean-demand single-insertion minimum at uniform ADD prices. The demand and stationary contract differ; this result computes no competing number.
- [#1865](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1865) schedules commuting C3 scalar fanout rewrites in a selected word. This abstract dirty-output tariff example neither implements those rewrites nor changes their profile or ceiling.

The completion check read this account's seven other open PRs created since the advance CLAIM: #7511, #7512, #7513, #7515, #7516, #7517 and #7518. None studies this two-epoch common-value dirty-fanout tariff or computes a competing optimum. No extra computation checked another contribution, and no shared numerical disagreement was found. The related-work entries above remain the relevant open comparisons.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At unchanged head `61215d260af77caf6f6edaa4c4be055737520e5a`, [run 43442573607](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43442573607), [plan job 131943660589](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43442573607/job/131943660589), failed in `Onboarding helper tests`. I read the completed checks once and inspected the actual job log. It reports 760 tests, exactly one failure and 24 skipped. The exact failing test and assertion are:

```text
test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found
```

The assertion is at line 58 of `tests/test_research_current_status.py`. I read canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` directly: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. Those two files and the failing test are unchanged between the base and this head. The mismatch is inherited from main.

The dependent [package replay job 131946333557](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43442573607/job/131946333557) was skipped because `plan` failed. All passing mathematical and source-binding checks above remain local evidence; hosted CI executed no package replay.

I independently inspected the actual failed-job logs for rohanarun's [run 42905094314, job 130140894651](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314/job/130140894651) and dillona's [run 42903313790, job 130134720799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790/job/130134720799). Both show the same sole failing test, missing-command assertion, 760-test total and 24 skips. No fix, retrigger commit, push, shared-file edit or workflow rerun was made. Maintainers own the repair of main.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. The seven isolated package files can be reverted together.

Blast Radius: research. No shared code, selected certificate or frozen predecessor file changes.
